title: Introduction to Angular Router knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Introduction to Angular Router”?
options: Introduction to Angular Router means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Introduction to Angular Router removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Introduction to Angular Router should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Introduction to Angular Router helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Introduction to Angular Router helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Introduction to Angular Router is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “What client-side routing does” in this lesson?
options: Assume “What client-side routing does” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “What client-side routing does” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “What client-side routing does” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “What client-side routing does” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “What client-side routing does” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “What client-side routing does” under Introduction to Angular Router. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Introduction to Angular Router”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
